razonamiento: The architecture diagram shows Sunday Sky's Rendering as a Service (RaaS) pipeline. Video requests from user devices hit API Gateway, which forwards to a frontend Lambda function. The Lambda sends rendering tasks to an SQS queue pulled by EC2 spot instances inside an Auto Scaling Group. The EC2 instances immediately post a response to a second SQS queue, which the frontend Lambda reads to return a playlist link back to the user device. The EC2 instances render video segments and upload them to S3, which are served via CloudFront to the user devices. In addition, there are two management flows: a custom auto-scaling mechanism where EC2 instances push metrics to CloudWatch, polled by a scaling Lambda invoked by Step Functions every 15 seconds to adjust the ASG; and a spot interruption handler where CloudWatch triggers an interruption Lambda that instructs the specific EC2 instance to drain jobs.
nombre: Sunday Sky Rendering as a Service Architecture

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Configured with usage plans and API keys to control load

nodes.name: RAS Frontend Lambda
nodes.notes: Validates requests and returns playlist link

nodes.name: Rendering Instructions Queue
nodes.notes: Holds rendering instructions for engine instances

nodes.name: Response Queue
nodes.notes: Receives immediate responses polled by frontend Lambda

nodes.name: Rendering Engine Instances
nodes.notes: Spot instances across multiple AZs with diversified types

nodes.name: CloudFront
nodes.notes: Pulls video segments from S3 origin to play to user

nodes.notes: Consumes metrics and scales the Auto Scaling group

nodes.notes: Collects rendering metrics and issues spot interruption events
